scope: Post-result descriptive triage of the 32 development worlds only. Not confirmation, an intervention result, or evidence of a new mechanism. No model calls were made for this analysis.
independent_unit: World. Name swaps, Focus variants, fields and repeated questions remain dependent measurements within a world.

behavior.directional_replication_note: The old four-world pattern in which every disagreement hurt the first alias did not replicate. Both directions occur, with more second-only-wrong pairs here.

identity_format_and_validity.interpretation: Strict identity accuracy is 75 percent, but its 128 failures are not all clean wrong-ID selections. Do not silently extract IDs from explanations, regrade malformed answers, or claim the model universally understood identity.

wrong_coref_facts_and_same_query_identit.interpretation: Correct identity with wrong attributes exists conditionally, but not universally. These are repeated field measurements, not 439 independent identity tests; this dissociation already has close prior precedents.

absolute_id_prior_warning: 542 of 647 errors select C or D, despite counterbalanced target IDs and record order. A stable-ID preference remains a serious competing explanation. Four literal IDs do not establish generalization to arbitrary entity identifiers.
wording_scope: Both wordings have errors, but fact accuracy differs substantially: about 80.5 versus 63.4 percent. Wordings are assigned between worlds, so their difference is descriptive, not a within-world causal effect of wording alone.
focus_interpretation: The irrelevant Focus manipulation is crossed within worlds. Highlighting the unrelated alias reduces fact accuracy from about 77.6 to 64.4 percent. This supports context-sensitive interference, not proof that the model simply copies the Focus object's value.
lexical_interpretation: These marginal name differences are descriptive associations across worlds. They do not isolate a causal effect of a particular spelling or word meaning. Consistent-name-swap comparisons, not marginal rankings, are the relevant controlled diagnostic.

strong_donor_cohort.rule: Same world, name swap and Focus; donor co-referring alias correct on all three facts and its ID; recipient has at least one completed listed wrong-object fact. This is stronger than the behavioral feasibility gate and does not change that gate.
strong_donor_cohort.selection_note: These choices reproduce the fixed prospective hash rule without examining intervention outcomes. The initial screen alone cannot demonstrate transfer to color. One selected case has mixed natural shape/home errors; predicting a single wrong record across fields remains an untested reverse-intervention hypothesis.

existing_baseline_limits.interpretation: The mixture improves probability assignments but its unconditional most likely choice always remains the correct binding. Conditional wrong-object choice removes the true object using ground truth and must not be presented as prospective error prediction. Constant-ID policies are not mixture components; the majority-ID policy is only a separate comparison. Known retrieval accounts have not been ruled out.
existing_baseline_limits.future_exploratory_comparison: Fit stronger absolute-ID-prior and field/wording-dependent retrieval mixtures using development data only, then freeze the chosen model before opening confirmation results. Keep that work labeled exploratory; do not weaken existing gates or alter the fixed causal screen cohort.

bottom_line: Wrong-object errors and co-referring-name inconsistency reproduce across many fresh worlds, with enough strictly eligible cases for the bounded discovery screen. This is a credible behavioral phenomenon, not yet a mechanistic discovery. Strong ID, field and wording dependence substantially narrow the interpretation. A new causal explanation and untouched confirmation are still missing.
